blocks.explanation:
A difference of two tangents of fixed angles.
We must show it equals \(2\sqrt{3}\) without tables.
Plan: write each tan as \(\frac{\sin}{\cos}\), combine into one fraction; the top becomes \(\sin(75^{\circ} - 15^{\circ})\) and the bottom \(\cos 75^{\circ}\cos 15^{\circ}\) is found with the product formula.
steps:
Given: L.H.S. \(= \tan 75^{\circ} - \tan 15^{\circ}\).
To prove: L.H.S. \(= 2\sqrt{3}\).
Method: \(\tan\theta = \frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}\), \(\sin(\alpha - \beta)\) formula and \(2\cos\alpha\cos\beta = \cos(\alpha + \beta) + \cos(\alpha - \beta)\).

Write as one fraction
\[\text{L.H.S.} = \dfrac{\sin 75^{\circ}}{\cos 75^{\circ}} - \dfrac{\sin 15^{\circ}}{\cos 15^{\circ}}\]
\[= \dfrac{\sin 75^{\circ}\cos 15^{\circ} - \cos 75^{\circ}\sin 15^{\circ}}{\cos 75^{\circ}\cos 15^{\circ}}\]
Why: Common denominator \(\cos 75^{\circ}\cos 15^{\circ}\).

Divide
\[\text{L.H.S.} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}/2}{1/4}\]
\[= \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\times 4 = 2\sqrt{3} = \text{R.H.S.}\]
Why: Dividing by \(\frac{1}{4}\) is multiplying by 4.
